[Tue 2026-04-07 20:49 UTC] What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?

Write your answer to `answer.txt` in the workspace. Provide a concise, factual answer.

content.thinking:
The algorithm being described is **Timsort**. It's a hybrid, stable sorting algorithm derived from merge sort and insertion sort. It's in-place (requires O(n) extra space but works within the array), stable, and has:
- Worst-case: O(n log n)
- Best-case: O(n) (already sorted or nearly sorted data)

Wait - is Timsort truly "in-place"? It requires O(n) auxiliary space. Let me reconsider.

Actually, the question says "in-place" - Timsort uses O(n) extra space, so it's not strictly in-place.


Let me think about other stable, in-place sorting algorithms with these complexity characteristics. Block sort claims to be stable and in-place with O(n log n) worst-case and O(n) best-case, but that's not well-known. Reconsidering the criteria: merge sort is stable with O(n log n) worst-case, but not in-place; Tim sort has the right time complexity but uses O(n) space; binary insertion sort is stable and in-place but only O(n²) worst-case. The description really does fit Timsort best, even with the space complexity caveat.
